standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness, flatness and finite locally free morphisms
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, labels morphisms-definition-finite-locally-free (proof line 2836) and morphisms-lemma-finite-flat (proof line 2862); same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-finite-in-codimension-one (proof line 2849)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the criterion in dimension one that a dominant morphism from an integral curve to a regular curve is finite, and the equivalence between finite flat and finite locally free.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of torsion free modules over a discrete valuation ring and the pushforward of a flat pullback
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, label more-algebra-lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat, invoked at proof line 2858; Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-dim-affine-space (proof line 2854) and algebra-definition-ord (statement, proof line 2814); same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-finite-flat (proof line 2840)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows every local ring of Y at a closed point is flat over the discrete valuation ring at its image because it is a domain, and computes the pushforward of the pulled back divisor as the degree times the difference of the two point classes.

core_obligations: Reduce to the pushforward along q: using the diagram constructed from X and f over S = Spec(K), rewrite c_* div_X(f) as c'_* q_* div_Y(f), and dispose of the case where q(Y) is a closed point of P^1_K, since then div_X(f) = 0 (proof lines 2818-2833).

Assuming q is finite locally free of degree d, use div_Y(f) = [q^{-1}D_0]_0 - [q^{-1}D_infty]_0 = q^*([D_0]_0 - [D_infty]_0) together with the pushforward formula for finite flat morphisms to get q_* div_Y(f) = d([D_0]_0 - [D_infty]_0), which has c'-pushforward zero because the two point classes have the same image in Spec(K) (proof lines 2834-2842).

Prove that q is finite locally free: it is finite by the codimension one criterion since P^1_K is one-dimensional, and each local ring of Y at a closed point is flat over the discrete valuation ring at its image because it is a domain and q is dominant, whence finite flat, i.e. finite locally free (proof lines 2844-2862).
proof_roadmap: Replace the principal divisor on X by the pushforward of the one on the graph Y and reduce to the pushforward along q (proof lines 2818-2833).
Using finite local freeness, compute q_* div_Y(f) as the degree times the difference of the two point classes and see it die downstairs (proof lines 2834-2842).
Establish finite local freeness of q from finiteness in dimension one and flatness over a discrete valuation ring (proof lines 2844-2862).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the degree of a principal divisor on a one-dimensional integral scheme proper over a field: the sum of the residue degrees weighted by the orders of an invertible rational function is zero, equivalently c_* div(f) = 0 (statement lines 2801-2816, tag 02RU). The proof moves the computation to the graph Y of f inside a projective line bundle, reduces it to the pushforward along q : Y -> P^1_K, and must first show that q is finite locally free, which it does by the codimension one finiteness criterion together with the fact that a domain over a discrete valuation ring is torsion free hence flat. The finite-local-freeness argument and the pushforward computation are the substance, so the claim is H2.
